newsitem.title: USA: CBOT RICE ENDS SLIGHTLY HIGHER ON SHORT COVERING.
newsitem.headline: CBOT RICE ENDS SLIGHTLY HIGHER ON SHORT COVERING.

text.p: Short covering in CBOT rice futures buoyed that market to modest gains at the close on Wednesday, floor traders said.
"Short covering in September supported the market throughout the day," said one floor trader.
Traders also noted light speculative scaled-up selling.

Cash prices were said to be weakening somewhat following the U.S. Department of Agriculture's production forecast on Tuesday. USDA put 1997/98 (Aug/July) rice production at a healthy 182 million hundredweight (cwt).
"Millers and exporters are anxious to get some business going," said one floor trader.
Cooler weather in the U.S. Delta states have also helped to boost rice production in recent days, traders said.
Merrill Lynch was a noted buyer in the September contract, pit sources said.
Rice ended three to five cents per cwt higher with September up three at $9.65. Volume was estimated by CBOT at 350 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 400 lots.
